subject.title: Plugin install doesn't build native bindings — plugins with better-sqlite3 fail on Node 24 (ABI v137) with bindings file not found

question: Should managed npm plugin installs keep lifecycle scripts disabled and add an explicit trusted native-addon rebuild or doctor repair path, or should OpenClaw automatically rebuild native dependencies during install?
rationale: The source-level failure is valid, but the direct fix runs untrusted npm lifecycle scripts and would change an intentional plugin-install security boundary.

options.title: Guarded Rebuild And Doctor Flow
options.body: Keep `--ignore-scripts` as the default, detect missing native artifacts or declared native packages, and offer an explicit trusted rebuild or doctor fix with clear logs and tests.

options.title: Diagnostics Only
options.body: Warn or fail with actionable package-root guidance while leaving rebuilds to plugin publishers or operators.

options.title: Automatic Rebuild
options.body: Run targeted `npm rebuild` during managed plugin install and accept broader install-time code execution for native dependency compatibility.

recommendation.title: Guarded Rebuild And Doctor Flow
recommendation.body: Keep `--ignore-scripts` as the default, detect missing native artifacts or declared native packages, and offer an explicit trusted rebuild or doctor fix with clear logs and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The central choice is whether to change the plugin install script-execution hardening introduced in this history.
